notes:
Lead summary: small dev studio building a hosted AI feature set for B2B SaaS customers. Primary stack: Next.js on Vercel, LangChain for orchestration, LlamaIndex for doc ingestion & retrieval. Wants Redwood Hosted API as drop-in replacement for their current OpenAI calls.

Customer priorities / quotes: "We want something we can plug into our existing LangChain LLMChain and Agents without rewriting agents logic. Also need a Vercel-friendly streaming example (Edge functions) and LlamaIndex connector for embeddings."

Technical asks: streaming SSE for chat (prefer token streaming into client), guidance on SSE via Vercel Edge Functions, example for using Redwood SDK with LangChain LLM wrapper, example LlamaIndex connector using Redwood embeddings and async batch upload strategy. Recommended constraints: median latency target <300ms for short-turn chat, throughput ~10-20 rps during peak, cost sensitivity for embeddings (batching + compression suggestions).

POC scope: 2-week technical POC. Week 1: sample repo + adapter PR, basic chat + streaming demo. Week 2: run small embed import (2k docs), verify retries/batching, measure per-token cost.

Support notes / ops: they've hit 429s on bulk embed import — want official guidance and example code with exponential backoff and batching size defaults. Ask from customer: "Can you share a minimal LangChain adapter and a LlamaIndex connector that use Redwood's hosted embeddings endpoint and show how to stream answers to a Next.js client?"

Sales/contract: SMB ARR expectations low-to-medium; likely start with pay-as-you-go hosted plan and scale to committed dedicated only if latency/cost justify.

Next steps (internal): prepare two example repos (langchain-adapter, llamalist-connector), a Vercel quickstart with streaming, and an FAQ on streaming billing vs non-streaming token accounting. Schedule pairing session week of 2026-03-15.

Stated blockers: adapter code + clear streaming billing explanation + bulk-embed retry examples.
